references.text: Ecclesiastes writes that God will bring every deed into judgment, including everything hidden—this is the background for the idea that what is hidden will be revealed.
Jesus says in Matthew that there is nothing covered that will not be uncovered, and nothing hidden that will not be made known—an almost identical parallel statement.
Jesus warns that people will give an account for every careless word they have spoken, emphasizing that all that is hidden will be made known.
The Markan parallel to this verse: Nothing is hidden except that it should be revealed, and nothing is secret except that it should come to light.
Later in Luke, Jesus repeats the same principle: There is nothing covered that will not be uncovered, and what has been said in darkness will be heard in the light.
Paul writes about the day when God will judge the hidden things of people—what is hidden will then be revealed.
Paul urges not to judge before the time, for the Lord will bring to light the hidden things of darkness and reveal the counsels of the heart.
Everything that is exposed by the light becomes visible, for everything that is made manifest is light—this aligns with the idea that what is hidden will come into the light.
